title: Berge–Fulkerson conjecture
formal: Does every finite loopless bridgeless cubic multigraph G have an ordered list \((M_{1},\ldots ,M_{6})\) of perfect matchings such that for every edge \(e\in E(G), |\{i\in \{1,\ldots ,6\}:e\in M_{i}\}|=2\)?
definitions: Edges of a multigraph have distinct identities and may share their unordered pair of endpoints; loops are forbidden. Cubic means every vertex has degree three, counting incident edge identities with multiplicity. A bridge is an edge whose deletion increases the number of connected components, and bridgeless graphs have none. Disconnected graphs are allowed. A matching is a subset of edges no two of which share an endpoint. It is perfect if every vertex is incident with exactly one of its edges. The six matchings may repeat; membership counts positions in the list, not just distinct subsets. The conclusion requires every edge to occur exactly twice, with no omitted edge and no extra coverage. No algorithmic bound is required.
answer_criterion: Prove the proposition in the problem statement or its logical negation with the stated model, hypotheses and quantifier order. The proof must settle the entire target. A result conditional on an additional assumption settles only that conditional version. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete proof checked by a proof assistant and matching this statement.
why: Ask whether every bridgeless cubic graph has a uniform six-term integral realization of its fractional perfect-matching structure.

importance.reason: A classical exact decomposition conjecture at the intersection of matching theory and global graph structure.

references.locator: Abstract and introduction: finite conjecture and relation to infinite cubic graphs
references.title: On some perfect matching conjectures in infinite, cubic, bridgeless graphs
references.authors: Júnior, Paulo Magalhães; Silva, Antonio Kelson

progress.text: Magalhães Júnior and Silva explicitly retain the finite conjecture as open while investigating its infinite analogues and their equivalences.

context_blocks.text: A single perfect matching chooses one incident edge at each vertex. Six such choices would give six incidences at every vertex; the conjecture asks for those incidences to be distributed evenly across its three edges.

The requirement is stronger than merely covering the edges with some collection of perfect matchings. Both the number six and exact multiplicity two belong to the target, and repeated matchings must be permitted.

The 2026 paper distinguishes the finite conjecture and its weaker matching-cover assertions while studying infinite graphs. A statement about a different cover object, such as a cycle double cover, does not establish this exact perfect-matching decomposition.

sentences: Every bridgeless cubic multigraph is asked to admit six perfect matchings.
Each edge must occur in exactly two positions of that six-matching list.
The matchings may repeat, and parallel edges remain distinct.
The target is an exact integral decomposition rather than an approximate or fractional cover.
It captures a longstanding structural question about how perfect matchings fit together globally.

status_note: Reviewed through 11 September 2026. The July 2026 primary preprint explicitly states that the finite conjecture remains open. No subsequent resolution was located; proofs in the cited preprint were not independently checked.

notes: Allowed repeated perfect matchings and made multiplicity and multigraph conventions explicit.
